data.cultural_impact: The name Prasen holds cultural significance in Hindu traditions as it is believed to be derived from the Sanskrit root "pras" meaning "bestow" or "give". The name signifies the act of bestowing blessings or grace upon an individual. In Hindu society, receiving a Prasad (blessed food offering) after a prayer or ritual is a common practice. Thus, the name Prasen reflects an individual who is bestowed with grace, blessings, and good fortune from the gods or the Universe.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Prasen holds immense significance as it is believed to be a reflection of God's mercy and grace. The name symbolizes the idea that one is not alone in their journey of life but is constantly surrounded by the benevolent presence of the divine. It serves as a reminder that even in times of hardship and adversity, one can turn to the gods for guidance, support, and ultimately, the gift of grace and mercy. Thus, the name Prasen is a reminder of the inherent connection between the individual and the divine, and the continuous flow of grace and mercy that nourishes and sustains all beings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Gift, Grace, Mercy" symbolizes Bestowing grace, Gift of the gods, God's mercy. In Hindu spirituality, bearing the name Prasen serves as a constant reminder of one's dharma and connection to Hindu values of gift, grace, mercy.

historical_references.reference: Prasenajit was the king of Magadha, who ruled around 480 BCE. He is mentioned in Buddhist texts as a friend and patron of Buddhism.
Prasenajit was also the name of a king of the Vatsa kingdom around 210 BCE, who was a contemporary of Ashoka. He is mentioned in the Ashoka inscriptions as a vassal king.
